data.aac#AAC (on main, not yet in a release):
Everything in this section is on the main branch of decode and is not in a release: the last release, v0.5.4, does not decode AAC. A release waits on speed parity with ffmpeg for 5.1 streams.
AAC-LC, written in Go from ISO/IEC 14496-3 (mono to 7.1, 8 to 96 kHz; M/S and intensity stereo, perceptual noise substitution, TNS, pulses, short windows), output f32le. Main, LTP, SSR, 960-sample frames, coupling channels and channel configurations 11, 12 and 14 are refused with ErrAudioUnsupported. HE-AAC v1 (SBR over AAC-LC) decodes at twice the core rate, whether the AudioSpecificConfig signals it or the stream only carries it. SBR in its downsampled mode is refused. Gapless: an MP4’s iTunSMPB item and edit lists are applied to AAC as ffmpeg does. DecodeAudioTrack applies it, NewAudioTrack does not. Parametric Stereo (HE-AAC v2) is not a supported output. The parser, the hybrid filter bank and the mixing are in the tree but switched off by default; a mono core that signals SBR is announced as stereo, its second channel a copy of the first, until Parametric Stereo is enabled. Checked: the error against a float64 reference of the same bitstream is about half of ffmpeg’s on the five fixtures; HE-AAC is within 3e-6 of ffmpeg 9.0.2 on four; 12 of the 15 ISO/IEC 14496-26 conformance vectors pass. Speed against ffmpeg is not measured yet. The README of decode states each of these with its conditions.
data.audio#Audio:
id, _ := decode.FirstAudioTrack(r) pcm, err := decode.DecodeAudioTrack(r, id, decode.AudioConfig{}) for _, a := range pcm { // presentation order, trimmed as the container states use(a.Data, a.Format, a.SampleRate, a.Channels, a.Layout, a.PTS) } NewAudioTrack streams it with DecodeSample and Flush. Data is interleaved little-endian PCM (s16le, s32le or f32le). The start of the track is dropped as its container states it (edit list, Opus pre-skip).
Codec Library Output Checked against ffmpeg FLAC mewkiz/flac s16le up to 16 bits, s32le up to 24 bit-exact on 13 fixtures MP3 (Layer III) tphakala/go-mp3 f32le maximum error 1.07e-6 on 10 fixtures, sample counts equal Opus pion/opus f32le, 48 kHz passes opus_compare on all 12 RFC 8251 test vectors, mono and stereo FLAC: 4 to 24 bits, 1 to 8 channels; a 32-bit stream is refused with ErrAudioUnsupported. MP3: MPEG-1, 2 and 2.5, mono and stereo. MP2 (Layer II) is not decoded and is refused with ErrAudioUnsupported. Opus: mono and stereo (mapping family 0); more channels (for example 5.1) are refused with ErrAudioUnsupported. Opus is checked against the RFC 8251 conformance vectors, not against ffmpeg’s output sample for sample. Vorbis is not decoded: the one pure-Go decoder tried failed the comparison with ffmpeg, and no decoder was written.
data.decode#decode: github.com/go-avkit/decode (latest release v0.5.4) decodes H.264 and HEVC / H.265 (Main and Main 10, 4:2:0) to planar YUV and FLAC, MP3 and Opus to PCM, in pure Go with no cgo. Vorbis and MP2 are not decoded; AAC is on the main branch and not in a release. H.264 is decoded by oops1/go.264 (BSD-2-Clause), pinned and forced onto its software path; HEVC by gen2brain/h265 v0.2.4 (MIT). decode is the avkit-facing layer around them and the place where claims are measured. It is the only module in this organisation that produces pictures or sound.
data.edit-lists#Edit lists:
Since v0.5.0, DecodeTrack and PosterFrame apply an MP4 track’s edit list by default, as ffmpeg does: a picture presented before an edit’s media time, or at its end or after, is decoded but not returned, presentation times are shifted so the pictures of the edit start at 0 (or at the length of the empty edit that delays the track), and PosterFrame’s t is a presentation time. This is a change from v0.3.0 for a file whose edit list trims or delays the track. Config.IgnoreEditList (ffmpeg’s -ignore_editlist 1) returns every picture labelled with track time, as v0.3.0 did.
An edit list the package does not apply is refused with ErrEditList rather than guessed at (a media rate other than 1, an edit lasting to the end of the media, an empty edit after the first edit that shows media, a media time before the track). Matroska has no per-track video edit list, so the first picture’s time is now 0, as in ffmpeg. Known divergence: for a fragmented MP4 with a trimmed start, ffmpeg and decode return different pictures (21 against 19 on the fixture), because ffmpeg switches its edit list support off for a fragmented file and decode cannot tell the file is fragmented yet (go-avkit/decode#20).
data.limits#Limits: A stream is untrusted. Config.MaxFrameMBs (default 36864, a 4096x2304 picture) and MaxSampleBytes (default 64 MiB) are checked before anything sized by the stream is allocated. Bomb tests assert a refusal under a memory limit for both video codecs, and the parsers and sample decoders are fuzzed with a committed corpus. AudioConfig limits the channel count, the block size, a coded sample and the PCM a track may return. PosterFrame has bounds of its own in PosterConfig: MaxSamples (default 600) caps the samples decoded for one picture, past it the error is ErrPosterLimit, and MaxTrackSamples (default 1«20) refuses a longer sample list.
data.measured#How it was measured:
Every picture’s MD5 is compared with ffmpeg’s -f framemd5, single thread.
ITU-T H.264.1 conformance suite (AVCv1): 81 streams tried, 73 give the same pictures as ffmpeg. 69 do with go.264 v1.12.0 as pinned; 4 more (MR2 to MR5_TANDBERG) only with the upstream fix oops1/go.264#2, which is merged upstream and not yet in a release. The other 8 are not claimed: 5 interlaced and 3 using FMO/ASO. JCT-VC conformance suite HEVC_v1 (ITU-T H.265.1): 147 streams. 143 give the same pictures as ffmpeg. Three are decided by the suite’s own MD5 because ffmpeg disagrees with it and decode agrees with it (SAODBLK_A_MainConcept_4, SAODBLK_B_MainConcept_4, VPSSPSPPS_A_MainConcept_1). One, TSUNEQBD_A_MAIN10_Technicolor_2 (luma and chroma bit depths differ), is refused by decode and by ffmpeg. The bitstreams are not in the repository, so the conformance test runs only when pointed at them. Streams and real files in the repository: 29 H.264 and 5 HEVC streams run in CI against ffmpeg’s MD5s; real MP4 and Matroska files (5 H.264, 7 HEVC) are recorded as hashes.
data.poster-frame#One picture: id, _ := decode.FirstVideoTrack(r) f, err := decode.PosterFrame(r, id, 12.5, decode.PosterConfig{}) PosterFrame (since decode v0.2.0) returns the picture with the greatest presentation time at or before t, the very bytes DecodeTrack returns for it, without decoding the whole track: decoding starts at the last sync sample at or before the picture’s sample and stops as soon as the picture is out. It takes H.264 (avc1, avc3) and HEVC (hvc1, hev1); another codec is ErrUnsupported. A negative or NaN t is ErrTime.
data.speed#Speed:
decode is slower than ffmpeg on every video input measured, and that is an open defect (go-avkit/decode#2). Measured on decode v0.3.0, single core, on an Apple M4 Max with ffmpeg 9.0.2 -threads 1, 5 interleaved rounds:
Input decode (fps) ffmpeg (fps) decode / ffmpeg H.264 High 1080p, real clip 36.5 173.1 0.21 HEVC Main 10 2160p, real clip 10.3 27.9 0.37 committed H.264 and HEVC streams 0.21 to 0.41 The profiles put the hot spots mostly in the wrapped libraries: go.264 has no arm64 assembly kernels, and gen2brain/h265 takes its assembly motion compensation at 8 bits only. The measurement is on arm64; an amd64 one is still needed. The audio decoders are not measured yet.
data.using-it#Using it: r, _ := container.NewReader(file) frames, err := decode.DecodeTrack(r, trackID, decode.Config{}) for _, f := range frames { // display order use(f.Y, f.Cb, f.Cr, f.YStride, f.CStride, f.Width, f.Height, f.PTS) } H.264 input: an avcC record (decode.NewAVCC) or a TrackConfig (decode.NewTrack) with length-prefixed samples, fed with DecodeSample and ended with Flush; or a raw Annex B stream (decode.New, DecodeAnnexB). HEVC input: the same calls choose HEVC for a track whose sample entry is hvc1 or hev1; decode.NewHVCC takes an hvcC record, decode.NewHEVC takes in-band parameter sets, and DecodeAnnexB a raw .265 stream. Main 10 frames hold little-endian 16-bit samples. Output: frames in display order, with planes, strides, size, chroma format, bit depth and PTS.
data.what-it-decodes#What it decodes: Codec and profile State H.264 Constrained Baseline; Baseline without FMO/ASO bit-exact H.264 Main, progressive (CAVLC, CABAC, B pictures, weighted prediction, multiple and long-term references, MMCO) bit-exact H.264 High, 4:2:0 8-bit, progressive bit-exact on the streams measured; no JVT FRExt stream measured yet H.264 interlaced (PAFF, MBAFF), FMO/ASO, Extended refused with ErrUnsupported H.264 High 10, 4:2:2, 4:4:4, lossless refused with ErrUnsupported HEVC Main, Main Still Picture, 4:2:0 8-bit bit-exact against ffmpeg HEVC Main 10, 4:2:0 10-bit bit-exact against ffmpeg HEVC other chroma formats, other bit depths, unequal luma and chroma depths refused with ErrUnsupported

Module Reference avkit pkg.go.dev bitstream pkg.go.dev boolcoder pkg.go.dev decode pkg.go.dev h264 pkg.go.dev h265 pkg.go.dev vp8 pkg.go.dev vp9 pkg.go.dev Descriptions live on the repositories themselves rather than being copied here, so there is one place to correct when one changes.
This table is kept by hand, and it had fallen six modules behind — it listed avkit alone while the organisation held seven. To check it, ask the organisation which of its repositories are Go modules:
for r in $(gh repo list go-avkit --limit 60 --json name --jq '.[].name'); do gh api repos/go-avkit/$r/contents/go.mod --jq '.name' >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "$r" done | sort
